title: Composition and refinement-pasting of actual etale normalized mates
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Work in ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. All schemes are Noetherian, meaning they admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For separated etale finite-type arrows $a$ and their composites [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] [def-weil-etale-morphism], choose compactifications [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $F_a=Ra_!\dashv G_a$, with counit $\varepsilon_a$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})\dashv a^*$ with counit $\operatorname{ev}_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Let $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ be the actual proper-support/sum comparison [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], and $\rho_a=(d_a^{-1})^c:G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. For composable $e:U\to X$, $v:X\to T$, let $\alpha:F_vF_e\to F_{ve}$ be the specified proper/open compositor [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], let $c_{v,e}:G_{ve}\to G_eG_v$ be its conjugate using the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and let $\kappa:(ve)^*\to e^*v^*$ be canonical pullback composition. Then
$$\kappa_K\circ\rho_{ve,K}=e^*(\rho_{v,K})\circ\rho_{e,G_vK}\circ c_{v,e,K}$$
for every $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. For identity arrows, $\rho$ is the canonical comparison with the identity functor. These equalities agree under the canonical proper-refinement comparisons for all chosen compactifications, with the right adjoints compared by their adjunction conjugates.

For an arbitrary Cartesian base change of an etale $e:U\to X$ by $w:X'\to X$, denote the resulting arrows by $e':U'\to X'$, $w':U'\to U$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $C_{e,w}:w^*F_e\to F_{e'}w'^*$ be the actual compact-support exchange from the same unbounded-comparisons node. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $B_{e,w,K}:w'^*G_eK\to G_{e'}w^*K$ be the adjunct of $w^*\varepsilon_{e,K}\circ C_{e,w,G_eK}^{-1}$. For a further morphism $z:X''\to X'$ of Noetherian schemes, write $e'':U''\to X''$ and $z':U''\to U'$ for its base change. With canonical pullback-composition identifications [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact],
$$B_{e,wz,K}=B_{e',z,w^*K}\circ z'^*B_{e,w,K}.$$
These maps and the composition equalities above agree under proper refinement and under arbitrary further Cartesian restriction by an open immersion. In particular, write $\chi^{w}_K:w'^*e^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}e'^*w^*K$ for the canonical pullback-composition map of the square of $w$, and similarly $\chi^{z}$, $\chi^{wz}$; then $\chi^{wz}_K=\chi^{z}_{w^*K}\circ z'^*\chi^{w}_K$ under the same identifications. Consequently, if $\rho_{e',w^*K}\circ B_{e,w,K}=\chi^{w}_K\circ w'^*\rho_{e,K}$ and $\rho_{e'',z^*w^*K}\circ B_{e',z,w^*K}=\chi^{z}_{w^*K}\circ z'^*\rho_{e',w^*K}$, then $\rho_{e'',(wz)^*K}\circ B_{e,wz,K}=\chi^{wz}_K\circ(w'z')^*\rho_{e,K}$ is obtained from them by this pasting.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-etale-support-sum-compositor] to the three arbitrary compactifications. It identifies the specified proper/open compositor alpha followed by the constructed graph comparison d_ve with the horizontal composite of d_e,d_v followed by the exact derived nested-sum compositor sigma. Invert the two graph comparisons horizontally and cancel their horizontal composite to obtain sigma followed by d_ve inverse equal to the horizontal inverses followed by alpha. The sum-composition-counit theorem identifies the conjugate of this specified sigma with the exact pullback compositor of [def-pur-etale-exact-pullback-unit-composition-comparisons].

proof.text:
Apply adjunction conjugacy to the equality in Step 1. Its reversal of vertical composition is [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]; the conjugate of the horizontal composite of the two inverse comparisons is, by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),
$$G_eG_v\xrightarrow{\rho_eG_v}e^*G_v\xrightarrow{e^*\rho_v}e^*v^*.$$
The conjugates of the remaining factors are $c_{v,e}$, $\rho_{ve}$ and $\kappa$, respectively. Thus the equality of conjugates is exactly
$$e^*\rho_v\,\rho_eG_v\,c_{v,e}=\kappa\rho_{ve}.$$
No inverse of $c_{v,e}$ is inserted: $\alpha$ points toward $F_{ve}$, so its conjugate points out of $G_{ve}$. For the identity clause, descend the ordinary sum-adjunction counit equation as a finite exact-derived pasting expression. Its conjugate is the specified exact pullback identity comparison. The identity clause of [lem-asd-compact-support-graph-coherence] identifies the graph comparison at the proper identity compactification. The already established rho refinement equation transports this comparison to arbitrary compactifications and right adjunctions.

proof.text:
For a proper-refinement comparison $t_a:F_a\to\widehat F_a$, [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] gives $d_a=\widehat d_a t_a$, and [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] gives
$$t_{ve}\alpha=\widehat\alpha\,(t_v*t_e).$$
Here $*$ denotes horizontal composition. Conjugating the first equation gives $\widehat\rho_a=\rho_a t_a^c$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Conjugating the second gives
$$c_{v,e}t_{ve}^c=(t_v*t_e)^c\widehat c_{v,e},$$
with the horizontal conjugate expanded by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2). Substitute these two equations into the composition identity of Step 2 and cancel the invertible refinement maps. This identifies its two sides with the two sides for the hatted choices. The cocycle and identity clauses of the unbounded-comparisons node make this independent of the common refinement, and also extend the identity normalization to every compactification. In the Lean proof, the refinement clause is an immediate application of EtaleSupportExchange.rightAdjointIso_refinement from [lem-pur-etale-support-exchange-right-mate], whose right-adjoint identification is definitionally this normalization. For the compositor-refinement clause, use the every-tower formula of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] to express each actual compositor through the common chosen compact-support functors. The comparison cocycle and naturality give alpha followed by t_ve equal to the horizontal comparison followed by alpha_hat. Conjugate this equality and expand horizontal conjugacy by the whiskerLeft and whiskerRight laws of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting].

proof.text: First use support_exchange_global to identify each transported exchange with unboundedEtaleCompactSupportBaseChange after the canonical compactification comparisons. Apply the composite-base-change equation of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]; naturality of the inverse-image compositors and the comparison maps cancels these maps and gives the forward pasting equation at the fixed compactifications. Invert it by cancellation. The private mates_paste lemma applies the final adjunction hom-bijection to the desired right-mate equation. The three mate counit identities, naturality of the intermediate inverse exchange and of the target pullback compositor reduce the two transposes to the inverted support pasting equation. Injectivity proves the result for every unbounded K. This is the counit calculation underlying [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting].

proof.text:
For refinement maps $t_e:F_e\to\widehat F_e$ and $t_{e'}:F_{e'}\to\widehat F_{e'}$, refinement compatibility of the actual exchanges in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] says
$$\widehat C\,w^*t_e=(t_{e'}w'^*)C.$$
Equivalently, $\widehat C^{-1}(t_{e'}w'^*)=(w^*t_e)C^{-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](3a),(3b), taking mates gives
$$(t_{e'}^c w^*)\widehat B=B(w'^*t_e^c).$$
Thus $B$ is unchanged under precisely the conjugate identifications of right adjoints required in the statement. The cocycle law for $t$ and the identity/composition laws for conjugacy show that this is independent of a common refinement. Substitution in Step 4 proves the same assertion for its pasted equality. In Lean, first identify each transported exchange with the compactification-independent base-change map using [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Its comparison cocycle gives the exchange-refinement square for arbitrary pairs of compactifications. Invert this square. Apply the adjunction hom-bijection and its counit equations to obtain the displayed right-mate refinement identity.

proof.text: Apply the sheaf-level vertical square-pasting equation [lem-weil-pbc-square-iso-pasting] to the flipped squares. A flipped square comparison is the inverse of the original comparison. Precompose with the inverse source pullback compositor and postcompose with the target pullback compositor; inverse cancellation yields the displayed inverse-square pasting equation on sheaves. Package all six sheaf categories and their exact inverse-image functors into finite words and the two routes into finite pasting expressions. Exactness is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Apply [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting] to the equality of their ordinary evaluations. Its prescribed word comparisons identify the derived square cells with exactDerivedSquareUpperStarIso.inv and the compositor cells with unboundedEtaleUpperStarCompIso.hom or .inv. Taking the component at an arbitrary unbounded derived object proves exactly the required pullback-pasting equation, with no bounded-below restriction. The complete calculation is extracted as the proved theorem [lem-pur-etale-exact-pullback-square-pasting] after profiling and local transparency improvements; the original clause applies it directly.

proof.text: For composition under arbitrary Cartesian restriction, use support_compositor_global and support_exchange_global to express every support map through the compactification-independent functors. The composition/base-change equation of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], with naturality and cancellation of the three comparison isomorphisms, gives W(alpha) followed by C_ve equal to C_v followed by F_v'(C_e) followed by alpha'. Invert the exchanges by cancellation. Apply the generic mate_refinement identity with comparison maps alpha and alpha', comparing the composite adjunctions with the single adjunctions. Expand the mate of the vertically pasted inverse exchanges with mateEquiv_hcomp of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Evaluation at K gives exactly B_ve followed by c' equal to w_U^*(c), then B_e at G_v(K), then H_e(B_v).

proof.text: For open restriction, prove the stronger normalization square for an arbitrary Cartesian square. The graph-comparison identification of [lem-asd-compact-support-graph-geometric-base-change] identifies the inverse constructed comparison with the existing compactificationEtaleComparison. Its base-change equation, transported through the exact/left-derived inverse-image isomorphisms, gives the square between the inverse support exchange and mapDerivedCategoryEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeIso. The graph comparison refinement identity of [lem-pur-etale-support-exchange-right-mate] transports its target to any compactification. The ordinary sheaf unit equation unit_map_etaleLowerShriekSquareBaseChangeMap_app identifies the ordinary sum exchange as the mate of the inverse pullback-square map. Write its counit transpose as two finite expressions in exact functors and descend their equality using [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting]. The descended counit cells are the counits of the specified onDerivedCategory adjunctions, so their hom-bijection identifies the mate of the exact sum exchange with the inverse exact pullback-square map. This avoids replacing the specified adjunction by the differently constructed mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction. Apply mate_refinement to the two inverse graph comparisons and the support/sum exchange square. Its conjugates are exactly rho and rho', so the resulting equation is the required normalization square, in particular for every open immersion. The exact sum mate calculation is implemented as the proved standalone theorem [lem-pur-etale-exact-sum-base-change-mate], to keep each module within the compile-time limit.
